entry.title: v2.0.0 (unreleased): one hosted backend, the Everyone board
entry.content:
v2.0.0 (unreleased): one hosted backend, the Everyone board

The directory holds exactly two crew-server names — both Sam's. Nobody
else ever registered one. So the crew-server layer goes, and with it
most of yesterday's crew-scoping work: simplicity is the product rule.

Removed: custom Firebase projects, the server directory (server_names,
servers), registration, join-by-name+code, custom names, renames, the
founders' rules dialog and the shipped rules copy, crew keys and
memberships, server.json. The add-on talks to one hosted project; an
old server.json is retired on profile open (a custom-project one signs
the user out so they can sign in again here).

Added — the Everyone board (rules-v4, NOT deployed):
- boards/{day}/rows/{uid}: one row per sharer per local day. Reading
  requires the reader to be sharing (symmetric, enforced); writing
  requires the writer to be sharing, the day id shape, and only the
  allowed fields with a non-negative reviews int.
- The view is bounded, never a full listing: top 50 by reviews via a
  single-field orderBy, plus three aggregations (people, reviews sum,
  rows above me) for the "2,381 studying today · 1.2M reviews together"
  headline and your rank. Plain #N ranks, no medals, no cheers; Add on
  the card. Old rows age out with the daily cleanup.
- Knocks are back to the simple shape: both people on the board.
- The v1.8–1.9 server_board collection is closed (owners may delete;
  the client does, once). Markers stay cumulative; RULES_MARKER is v4.
- The footer's rules notice is informational ("server catching up") —
  only the maintainer deploys rules now.
- Shares keep their approved formats; the crew tape's header comes from
  a local "Crew name in shares" setting (crew_label) since servers are
  gone.

Tests: fake backend restates the v2.0 rules (parent-path queries,
aggregations, method- and field-aware writes); 68 checks green.
tests/rules/ emulator test rewritten for the global rules — still NOT
executed here. Docs: README (hosted backend, Everyone board, no
crew-server section), CLAUDE.md, config.md, checklist, tests README.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: v1.10.0 (unreleased): crew-scoped server privacy, honest shares, scop…
entry.content:
v1.10.0 (unreleased): crew-scoped server privacy, honest shares, scoped styling, tracked tests

Privacy — rules-v4 (NOT deployed; see docs and the report):
- The server board and knocks were scoped only client-side: rules gated
  reads on the reader's own openBoard flag, the row's `server` field was
  client-written, and knocks needed only two openBoard flags. Any sharer
  on the shared project could list every crew's rows and knock anyone.
- Boundary, now explicit: a crew is the set of accounts holding a
  membership doc under a crew key = sha1(name:code), the capability the
  directory already uses. Rows live at servers/{key}/board/{uid}; reads
  require membership AND sharing; row writes require membership; knocks
  name the crew and need both memberships. Membership is created by
  path — nothing freely editable decides it. Aliases (renames) point a
  new name at an existing crew via `crewKey` on the servers doc; members
  who joined before v1.6 enter their code once (CrewCodeDialog).
- The unscoped server_board collection is closed to reads/writes; the
  client deletes its old row once. Markers stay cumulative
  (['rules-v2','rules-v3','rules-v4']); this is a breaking change for
  v1.8–1.9 clients' server board, whose tripwire fires on the next
  rejected write.

Shares — truthful:
- "cards" -> "reviews" (answer events). Hourly buckets are anchored on
  the Anki rollover, and day docs/rows carry `dayStart` so friends'
  hours are placed by absolute time on the viewer's day: "we covered N
  hours" is one shared timeline. People who studied but don't share
  hours are counted ("N not sharing hours"), never drawn as idle; a
  total missing hidden counts says "(partial)". Older clients' hours
  (no dayStart) are not misplaced — they are reported as unshared.

Styling — scoped:
- Dropped `body { overflow-x: hidden !important }` (page-wide). Dropped
  the `overflow: visible !important` cell rule that defeated the name
  column's ellipsis; the column now ellipsizes for real (verified with a
  long name at 480/400 px: zero table/card/page overflow). Kept: white /
  near-black card, no border, no shadow, no lines or fills inside the
  table except the personal-row highlight; Anki 26's `.fancy table`
  glass verified defeated in both themes.

Tests — reproducible:
- Harness moved to tests/ (repo-relative, stdlib only; 76 checks) with
  a fake that RESTATES rules-v4 and is labeled as such, plus
  tests/rules/ — an emulator-based rules test (crew scoping, consent,
  symmetric reads, retraction, retired collection, cumulative markers)
  that could not be executed here (no firebase-tools/Java). tools/
  preview.py renders every view/theme with Anki's glass rule for
  browser-side CSS checks.

Docs: README (privacy boundary, share semantics, testing), CLAUDE.md
(marker policy for breaking rules changes), docs/manual-anki-checklist.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: v1.9.1: shares survive the clipboard — UTF-8 all the way to the paste
entry.content:
v1.9.1: shares survive the clipboard — UTF-8 all the way to the paste

Copied shares came out as '?' for every emoji and block glyph, and '∑'
for '·' — the signature of text squeezed through Latin-1 with '?'
replacement and read back as Mac Roman. That is Qt's legacy
"traditional Mac plain text" pasteboard flavor, which some paste targets
pick over the UTF-8 one.

- ui/__init__.py gains copy_text(): on macOS, pbcopy under a UTF-8
  locale (writes only the UTF-8 flavor, nothing lossy to grab); on
  failure or other platforms, Qt with explicit text/plain;charset=utf-8
  mime data, then plain setText as the last resort.
- Every clipboard write in the add-on goes through it — the three
  shares, the wrap copy, friend code, invite, server name+code, and the
  rules paste. Direct QApplication.clipboard().setText calls are gone.
- Tests cover both paths (63 checks).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: v1.9: the share pack — paste-ready days for the group chat
entry.content:
v1.9: the share pack — paste-ready days for the group chat

Three copies, designed glyph by glyph with Sam:

- Crew today: everyone's study hours side by side as an emoji tape
  (12 two-hour slots, ⬜🟨🟩), names trailing so the edge stays aligned
  in any chat font, ordered by who started the day. Absence is silent —
  only people who studied today get a row. Today view footer → Share.
- My today, sparkline: 24 hourly slots as blocks (░ idle, ▁..█ scaled
  to the day's peak) between an effort line (cards, time) and an
  identity line (🔥 streak, 🎯 retention).
- My today, tape: the same day as 🌅/🌙 rows of hourly squares.
  Both live on your own profile card: "Copy for the chat: today · tape".

Every share signs off "— Due Crew · Anki add-on 2035408484".

Data: the daily doc gains `hours`, a 24-character intensity string
written by the same upload under the share_time toggle (off deletes
it, like every metric). daily_stats has no field whitelist, so the
rules-v3 paste already covers it — no rules change. Friends' tapes
read that field; your own row comes from local revlog, always fresh.
share.py is pure text with no network or collection access; the
clipboard copy rides pycmd like every other copy in the add-on.

entry.title: v1.8.5: crew renames — the console writes it once, every member follows
entry.content:
v1.8.5: crew renames — the console writes it once, every member follows

A crew outgrowing its generated name (breezy-newt-6261 → busm) couldn't
actually rename: the name lives in each member's local server.json,
written at join and never re-read. Now the directory can carry the
rename and the fleet follows it:

- The founder registers the new name in-app, then adds a `renamedTo`
  string field to the OLD server_names doc in the Firebase console.
  No rules change: server_names is client-create-only, so only the
  project owner can write that field — renames stay hijack-proof.
- Each member's add-on checks its server's doc once a day (riding the
  rules-probe cadence, one world-readable GET), follows up to three
  chained hops, adopts the new name on the main thread, and says so
  with a tooltip. The label, invites, and the server-board scope all
  travel together. The stored join code belonged to the old name, so
  it's dropped; invites use the short form until the founder shares
  the new code.

entry.title: v1.8: server board, knocks, custom crew names — rules-v3
entry.content:
v1.8: server board, knocks, custom crew names — rules-v3

The community push. A server (with v1.7's custom-name provisioning now
built: founders type "busm" at registration, first come, first named)
gains an opt-in board of everyone sharing on it:

- Server pill, fifth on the board. Not sharing? An opt-in card — sharing
  goes both ways and there is no peeking, enforced by rules (reading
  server_board requires your own openBoard flag).
- One compact public row per sharer (server_board/{uid}: name, server,
  day, reviews, time, streak), through the hash-guarded upload — +1
  write per sync. The view is lazy: one equality-only query on open
  (no composite index for founders), cached minutes, client-sorted.
  Today-only; absence is silent.
- Deliberately spare with strangers: plain #N ranks, no medals, no
  cheers, no celebration surfaces. Weeks, days, decks, heatmaps, and
  profile depth stay crew-only.
- Adding lives on the card, not the row: click a name, the spare
  stranger card offers "Add to crew". That writes YOUR friends array
  and a knock (cheers-shaped doc, sharers-only by rule); they see
  "wants to be crew — Add back" in Friends and one click makes it
  mutual. Ignore deletes the knock and mutes re-knocks locally.
  Nobody ever writes anyone else's friends array.
- Knock names render from profiles, not the doc — senders can't spoof.
- Account deletion sweeps the public row and knocks.
- Rules markers are now CUMULATIVE (['rules-v2','rules-v3']) so v1.7
  clients stay green on v3 rules; RULES_MARKER bumps to rules-v3 and
  the v1.7 tripwire rolls the paste out to existing founders.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: v1.7: welcome back, duet days, exam-eve assist, crew milestones, rule…
entry.content:
v1.7: welcome back, duet days, exam-eve assist, crew milestones, rules tripwire

Four crew features, zero extra document reads, plus the drift detector:

- Welcome back: the day a quiet friend's first sync lands after 7+ days,
  one toast with the true gap and a 👋 chip on their row for that day.
  Spoken to the crew, never at the returner — no "you were gone" copy
  exists. Local prev-state in wrap.json.
- Duet days: the profile card names the thing only a friendship can
  have — current and best runs of days both people studied, computed
  from the heatmap doc the card already fetches, with a two-row week
  strip. Appears only when their heatmap is shared.
- Exam-eve assist: the day before a crew member's shared exam, one
  dismissible amber line above the board with the 💪 pre-aimed.
  Multiple exams merge into one line, never a stack.
- Crew milestones: weekly wrap totals accrue into lifetime crew
  numbers; crossings (100k/250k/500k/1M reviews, 1,000 hours) toast
  once, join that week's banner and its Copy. Whole-crew only — there
  is no per-person ladder.
- Rules tripwire: firestore.rules now carry a generation marker
  (meta/rules-v2, get-only, no data); the client probes it once a day
  and flips instantly on any rejected write. While stale, the board
  footer shows "Server rules need an update" opening a dialog with the
  console steps and a one-click copy of the shipped rules text
  (due_crew/firestore.rules, kept identical to the root file).
- Rules also provision custom crew names (proposed, unbuilt): size
  floor 3, charset pinned, optional `custom` flag on server_names — so
  that feature can ship later without another founder paste.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: v1.6.1: truthful dots, loud upload failures, one radius language
entry.content:
v1.6.1: truthful dots, loud upload failures, one radius language

- Days view told the truth badly: a day only existed server-side if a
  sync ran while it was "today", so a long streak could sit beside a
  half-empty dot row. Syncs now backfill the week's studied days,
  hash-guarded per day — a no-change sync writes nothing, steady state
  stays at most one daily write per sync.
- Day docs carry a numbers-free `studied` flag (shared unless paused),
  so a friend who shares no numbers still shows up in Days. _showed()
  prefers it; docs from older versions keep the metric fallback.
- Rejected writes print their path and status instead of failing
  silently — a silent False in patch_doc hid the heatmap rules gap.
  Heatmap retraction keys on a deleted marker so a fresh sign-in with
  sharing off still clears a stale doc, exactly once.
- Privacy saves push immediately (upload + refetch) instead of waiting
  for the next sync; _on_sync_done gathers independently so one failure
  can't silently stop the rest.
- UI: the board is a framed 12px surface like its loading/signed-out
  cards; the you-row is the spec's lozenge; tables scroll inside the
  frame on narrow windows instead of bleeding past the corner; pills
  full-round; deck counts stopped wrapping; Qt accent/danger colors
  follow night mode; the friend code got the spec's well treatment.

Streak base scan is bounded to 60 days per sync (full history still
cached once per day), so huge collections don't pay per sync.
